title: Chapter 3.  History — From Portuguese Colonies to Indian Union Territory

blocks.content: History is the richest and most distinctive chapter for DNH&DD, because both halves of the UT share an unusual Portuguese colonial past that lasted far longer than British rule elsewhere in India — Goa, Daman and Diu were only integrated into India in 1961, fourteen years after Independence. Expect detailed questions on Operation Vijay, the annexation of Dadra & Nagar Haveli, and the sequence of administrative changes since.
Portuguese Colonial Period

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Dadra and Nagar Haveli were liberated from Portuguese colonial rule in 1954.
Operation Vijay was executed in 1961 to annex Goa, Daman, and Diu into the Indian Union.
The territories evolved from 'Goa, Daman and Diu' into separate Union Territories, followed by a re-merger in 2020.

blocks.content: Daman and Diu were captured by the Portuguese in the 16th century — Diu in 1535 (ceded by the Sultan of Gujarat, Bahadur Shah, as part of an alliance against the Mughals) and Daman in 1559 — and remained under continuous Portuguese rule for over four centuries, making them, along with Goa, the last European colonial possessions on Indian soil.

Dadra and Nagar Haveli came under Portuguese control later and through a different route: in 1779, the Maratha Peshwa government granted the Portuguese the right to collect revenue from 72 villages of Nagar Haveli as compensation for a warship, the 'Santana', that the Marathas had seized from the Portuguese but not returned — a treaty of friendship rather than outright conquest.

Together with Goa, Daman and Diu formed the 'Estado da India' (Portuguese State of India), each a separate administrative district, while Dadra and Nagar Haveli functioned as a dependent territory administered from Daman.

cells: Ceded by Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat (alliance against the Mughals)
Treaty of friendship with the Maratha Peshwa (revenue-collection rights over 72 villages, as compensation for the seized warship 'Santana')

blocks.content: Liberation of Dadra and Nagar Haveli (1954)

Dadra and Nagar Haveli was 'liberated' from Portuguese rule seven years earlier than Daman and Diu, through a local pro-independence uprising rather than a formal Indian military operation. On 22 July 1954, freedom fighters and volunteers of the 'Azad Gomantak Dal' and the United Front of Goans (with support from the Communist Party of India, RSS-linked organisers, and other nationalist groups) captured the territory from Portuguese administrators in a swift, largely bloodless action.

Following liberation, a self-governing 'Varishta Panchayat' (Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli administration) governed the enclave independently from 1954 to 1961, functioning almost as a free-standing mini-state, until it was formally integrated into the Indian Union.

On 11 August 1961, the Dadra and Nagar Haveli Act, 1961 (passed by Parliament) formally merged the territory into India as a centrally administered Union Territory, ending the seven-year interim self-governance period.

★ EXAM POINT: Dadra & Nagar Haveli's path to India was DIFFERENT from Goa/Daman/Diu — it was freed by a local popular uprising in 1954 and self-governed for 7 years before formal Indian integration in 1961, whereas Goa/Daman/Diu were annexed directly by the Indian Army in 1961's Operation Vijay. This distinction is a favourite exam trap.
Annexation of Goa, Daman and Diu — Operation Vijay (1961)

Portugal refused to negotiate the peaceful transfer of Goa, Daman and Diu despite growing international pressure and UN resolutions on decolonisation through the 1950s. After years of diplomatic stalemate, the Government of India launched a military action codenamed 'Operation Vijay' on 18-19 December 1961.

Indian armed forces (Army, Navy and Air Force in a coordinated tri-service operation) took control of Goa, Daman and Diu within roughly 36 hours, meeting only limited resistance; Portuguese Governor-General Manuel Antonio Vassalo e Silva formally surrendered on 19 December 1961.
Following the operation, Goa, Daman and Diu were administered together as a single, centrally administered Union Territory named 'Goa, Daman and Diu' from 1961 onward.

★ EXAM POINT: Operation Vijay (1961) refers to the annexation of Goa/Daman/Diu — do not confuse it with the later, more famous 'Operation Vijay' of the 1999 Kargil War; both share the same codename but are entirely different military operations decades apart.
From 'Goa, Daman and Diu' to Separate UTs, and the 2020 Re-Merger

In 1987, Goa was granted full statehood (becoming India's 25th state) via the Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987, while Daman and Diu were carved out and continued as a separate, smaller Union Territory of their own — 'Daman and Diu' — from 30 May 1987 onward.

items: Operation Vijay (1961) is a frequently asked code name associated with the integration of Goa, Daman, and Diu into India.
Remember the key chronological sequence: Dadra and Nagar Haveli Liberation (1954) preceded Operation Vijay (1961).
The re-merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu as a unified Union Territory took place in 2020.

blocks.content: Dadra and Nagar Haveli, meanwhile, had remained a distinct Union Territory since its 1961 integration, entirely separate from the Goa-Daman-Diu administrative unit throughout this period.

Both these separate UTs (Dadra & Nagar Haveli, and Daman & Diu) were then merged into the single present-day Union Territory of 'Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu' on 26 January 2020, as detailed in Chapter 1 — completing the territory's complex, multi-stage administrative history.

cells: Diu and Daman respectively come under Portuguese control
Dadra & Nagar Haveli comes under Portuguese revenue-collection rights via treaty with the Maratha Peshwa
Dadra & Nagar Haveli 'liberated' by local uprising; self-governed as free territory (Varishta Panchayat) 1954-61
Operation Vijay — Indian armed forces annex Goa, Daman and Diu from Portugal
Dadra & Nagar Haveli Act, 1961 formally integrates the territory into India as a UT
Goa, Daman and Diu administered together as a single UT
Goa becomes a full state (25th state of India); Daman and Diu continues as a separate, smaller UT
Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu merge into the present single UT, 'DNH&DD'

blocks.content: Quick Revision Points

items: Diu (1535) and Daman (1559) were Portuguese colonies for over 400 years; Dadra & Nagar Haveli came under Portuguese revenue rights via an 1779 treaty with the Maratha Peshwa.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli liberated by a local uprising on 22 July 1954; self-governed 1954-61; formally integrated into India via the Dadra and Nagar Haveli Act, 1961, on 11 August 1961.
Goa, Daman & Diu annexed by India in Operation Vijay, 18-19 December 1961 (not the same as the 1999 Kargil operation of the same name).
Goa became a full state in 1987 (Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987); Daman & Diu continued as a separate UT from 30 May 1987.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli (separate UT since 1961) and Daman & Diu (separate UT since 1987) merged into today's DNH&DD on 26 January 2020.
